headline: High: Haystack’s broad egress and MCP exposure can feed Prefect workflows with unverified outputs, creating default-path data leakage and cascading automation risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so its outputs can be bridged into Prefect workflows. Prefect is an orchestration tool, so if it ingests Haystack-produced content as task input, prompt-like instructions can propagate. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, but the bridge is not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Haystack output from a shared MCP server or API response without provenance checks, injection risk is present.
IF the operator manually copies Haystack text into Prefect task definitions, injection risk is present.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every Haystack output before Prefect reads it.
Require Prefect tasks to parse only structured JSON, not free text.
Disable MCP routes that accept arbitrary instruction-like payloads.
Review one end-to-end sample flow for instruction leakage.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call MCP servers; Prefect also has broad egress. Both touch non-sensitive metadata classes, but a shared workflow can still move Haystack context into Prefect outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so the main risk is default network-mediated leakage rather than local file exposure.
conditions: IF Haystack retrieves source documents containing sensitive fields and forwards them into Prefect-managed tasks, leakage is present.
IF Prefect logs task payloads to an external service, Haystack context can be exposed.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a test dataset for the first run.
Turn off verbose logging in Prefect for payload-bearing tasks.
Redact secrets and PII before passing Haystack output onward.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention at the workflow boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can call APIs and MCP servers, while Prefect is an orchestration layer with broad egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or database, so direct write contention is not evidenced. The interaction is plausible only if the operator wires both to the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or database, write conflict risk appears.
IF the operator points both agents at the same mutable workspace, contention risk appears.
mitigations: Assign separate output destinations for each agent.
Use read-only credentials where possible.
Check for duplicate writes in one dry run.
Serialize writes through a single queue.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control on shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent, so its outputs are likely to be treated as facts or retrieved context. Prefect is an automation/orchestration tool, so if it consumes Haystack output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream workflow actions. The profiles do not prove this exact pipeline, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Haystack output as authoritative task input without validation, cascading error risk is present.
IF Prefect triggers downstream jobs from Haystack-generated summaries, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any Prefect action.
Require confidence thresholds on Haystack outputs.
Compare Haystack results against a second source.
Log and diff the exact payload passed between agents.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before workflow execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only list anonymous usage statistics or workflow metadata as touched data classes, so no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch is shown. Haystack has broad egress, which could create compliance issues if sensitive data is introduced, but that is not evidenced here. Prefect’s profile does not show a conflicting residency or retention policy.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Haystack into Prefect, compliance review is required.
IF the operator enables retention of workflow payloads containing personal data, policy mismatch risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair for initial deployment.
Review retention settings in Prefect.
Disable payload logging where possible.
Document the data classes allowed through the workflow.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement.
